question.problem:
Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(8,10)=\frac{9}{10},\,F(8,8)=\frac{3}{5},\,F(8,4)=\frac{2}{5}.
$$

Find $P(X\le 8,4\le Y\le 8).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the probability that the pair $(X,Y)$ will lie inside the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axes.

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211556/assets/d31cdb5e3f201d9dd5b3b622d883f67bb2c8bc0a5036905695a5cc5ceb3bda07.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained by taking the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(8,8)$ (the blue region below) and *subtracting* the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(8,4)$ (the red region below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211556/assets/626d5c4cba7b41d6b6f2da77ca1d62c5bcd442990ce31cf630e69882dd6580b8.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 8,4\le Y\le 8) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(8,8)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 8,Y\le 8)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(8,4)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 8,Y\le 4)}} \\  & =F(8,8)-F(8,4) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}-\frac{2}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
